mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 250 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a C250 petrol typically costs between £600 and £4,800 depending on the engine code and condition. Used M271 units start from £600-£1,500, reconditioned from £1,800-£3,000, and fully rebuilt M274 engines from £2,500-£4,800. Labour for supply & fit adds £500-£1,000.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the M271 and M274 engines in the C250 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M271 is a 1.8-litre turbocharged four-cylinder engine used in the W204 C250 CGI (2011-2014), producing 204 hp with a single-row timing chain. The M274 is a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder engine used in the W205 C250 (2014-2018), producing 211 hp. The M274 replaced the M271 and offers more power and torque, but suffers from a wrist pin/piston seizure defect. The M271 is more prone to timing chain stretch and camshaft adjuster failure.

mainEntity.name: Does the C-Class 250 petrol have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the M271 and M274 engines use timing chains, not belts. The M271 uses a single-row timing chain that is considered a wear item - failure typically occurs between 60,000-100,000 miles. The M274 also uses a timing chain, but it is generally more robust than the M271's chain. A rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start is the classic warning sign for timing chain issues.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of engine problems in a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 250 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: On M271-equipped models (W204 C250 CGI, 2011-2014), the most common symptom is a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start, rough idle, hesitation, poor fuel economy, and power loss. On M274-equipped models (W205 C250, 2014-2018), symptoms include unusual engine noise, particularly on start-up, and potential sudden engine failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 250 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and condition. A W204 C250 CGI is typically worth £4,000-£9,000 - a rebuilt M271 engine (£2,200-£3,800) can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. A W205 C250 is worth £6,000-£15,000 - a rebuilt M274 engine (£2,500-£4,800) is usually well within the car's value. For the M274, a specialist replacement with an upgraded rebuilt unit is almost always better value than attempting to rebuild the original engine due to the wrist pin design flaw.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz C-Class 250 petrol to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the C250 petrol depends on the engine. On M271 engines, timing chain stretch can cause cam timing drift, reducing power. On M274 engines, the wrist pin/piston seizure failure can cause misfires and power loss. Other causes include camshaft adjuster failure (M271) and oil leaks affecting engine performance. A diagnostic check with Mercedes STAR or compatible equipment is essential to identify the exact cause.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 250 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The C250 petrol badge has represented the performance-oriented four-cylinder petrol option across two generations of the Mercedes-Benz C-Class. The W204 facelift introduced the C250 CGI with the M271 1.8-litre turbocharged engine, while the W205 generation adopted the larger M274 2.0-litre turbo unit. Both engines offered a compelling blend of performance and efficiency, positioned above the C180 and C200 and below the V6-powered C350.

M274.920, 2.0L turbo petrol, 211 hp (155 kW) - W205 C250 launch; 350 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 6.6 seconds; 7G-TRONIC automatic

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 250 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The C250 petrol has been powered by two distinct engine families - the M271 1.8-litre (W204) and the M274 2.0-litre (W205). The M271 is notorious for timing chain failure, while the M274 suffers from a wrist pin/piston seizure defect that led to an NHTSA investigation. Rebuilt C250 petrol engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components designed to address the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: M271 Timing Chain Failure - The W204 C250 CGI's Critical Weakness
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 250 petrol (M271.860 and M271.861, W204, 2011-2014)
problems.rootCause: The M271 uses a single-row timing chain that stretches prematurely, often combined with failing camshaft adjusters. Symptoms include a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start, rough idle, hesitation, poor fuel economy, and power loss. P0017 almost always points to a stretched timing chain or a failing camshaft adjuster. The M271 engine is an interference design - if the timing chain breaks or slips, valves and pistons hit and the engine is effectively junk.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, both camshaft adjusters
repairOptions.longevity: Best done at first rattle; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Cylinder head removal, valve replacement, piston inspection, full timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has slipped; bent valves almost certain

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete replacement with professionally rebuilt M271 unit with upgraded timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Best long-term value on higher-mileage cars

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W204 C250 CGI is worth £4,000-£9,000. For vehicles under £5,000, a preventative chain replacement (£1,100-£1,800) is usually the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For higher-value examples, a rebuilt M271 with warranty (£2,500-£4,200) offers peace of mind.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold starts - especially between 60,000 and 100,000 miles - act immediately. A preventative chain replacement at a specialist (£1,100-£1,800) saves thousands compared to waiting for failure. The M271 EVO engines have reduced failure rates compared to earlier M271s which used conventional roller chains, but the risk remains significant.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M271 Mercedes-Benz C250 petrol engine prices

problems.h4: M274 Wrist Pin / Piston Crack - The W205 C250's Hidden Failure
problems.rootCause: The M274 engine suffers from a wrist pin / piston seizure failure. The pin that connects the piston to the connecting rod seizes within the piston boss, causing the piston skirt to crack and cylinder bore scoring. Mercedes technical service bulletin (TSB) LI03.10-P-060916 addresses the wrist pin concern. A petition was submitted to NHTSA requesting an investigation into alleged "wrong-sized wrist pins" in Mercedes-Benz vehicles equipped with the M274 engine. The condition is attributed to unfavourable piston-wrist pin tolerance. Symptoms include unusual engine noise, particularly on start-up, and potential sudden engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: There is no known preventative repair for the M274 wrist pin fault - it is a design/manufacturing defect that manifests without prior warning signs
Single piston and wrist pin replacement, cylinder hone, new rings, cylinder head gasket replacement, oil system flush
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if compression loss caught immediately

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete replacement with professionally rebuilt M274 unit featuring upgraded pistons designed to address the wrist pin design flaw
repairOptions.longevity: Almost always the better financial decision on a W205

problems.recommendation: The M274 piston crack is a frustrating failure because there is no preventative fix. The first warning is often unusual engine noise or a misfire code. On a 2014-2018 W205 C-Class worth £6,000-£15,000, a specialist replacement with an upgraded rebuilt unit (£2,500-£4,800 fitted) is almost always better value than attempting to rebuild the original engine. Ensure any replacement engine specifically states it has upgraded wrist pin/piston components.

problems.group: M271 & M274 Oil Leaks & Camshaft Adjuster Issues
problems.h4: M271 & M274 Oil Leaks & Camshaft Adjuster Issues
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 250 petrol (M271.860/861 and M274.920, W204 and W205, 2011-2018)
problems.rootCause: Both M271 and M274 engines can suffer from oil leaks from valve cover gaskets and breather systems. The M271's camshaft adjusters can fail, causing rough running and timing issues. The M274 can suffer from camshaft adjuster solenoid issues and oil in the wiring harness.

repairOptions.longevity: Viable; prevents oil leaks from top of engine

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with new gaskets and adjusters
repairOptions.longevity: Only if engine damage has occurred

problems.recommendation: Regular inspection for oil leaks and addressing camshaft adjuster issues promptly can prevent more serious damage. If you notice oil spots under the car or hear unusual noises from the top of the engine, have the system inspected immediately.
